why: Controlled stress-test protocol, not a measured public-road exposure: every simulated trip includes exactly one H0 pedestrian outside the marked crosswalk, hence exposure = 1/1 = 1. Keep the surrounding traffic drawn from town B (world=town). The marked crosswalk is x=122 m in avsim/core.py; H0 is 18-38 m beyond it (x=140-160 m), so the experiment tests whether crossing anticipation generalizes beyond the hard-coded crosswalk. The ego lane centre is z=1.75 m and the south pavement is z=9.2 m: the pedestrian must cover 7.45 m. At the deliberately brisk but sub-2.5 m/s test speeds 1.8-2.4 m/s, that takes 3.10-4.14 s. A trigger gap of 26-36 m spans ego arrival times 2.17-4.50 s at 8-12 m/s, overlapping that crossing window. These are declared engineering test envelopes, sampled uniformly, not fitted human behaviour or occurrence rates. The exact scene x=145, v=2.2, trig=30 is a feasible avoidable collision found in a separate 36-scene design check; final probabilities come only from the fixed 1500-draw mine sweep. Rates multiplied by exposure describe this every-trip hazard protocol only and must not be claimed as natural town or real-road frequencies. A deployment estimate requires measured occurrences per trip for the intended route.
